observations: Visible scuffs and marks on the top matte surface of the console.
PS4 logo is visible on the front right of the unit in photo 0.
The console is shown powered off on a plastic chair.
Watermark 'MISHAEL JEREMIAH' is present across the image.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows the original model and two controllers.
Requires a clear photo of the warranty seals on the rear of the console.
Requires a video of the console running a demanding game for at least 10 minutes.
Requires testing of HDMI, USB, and power ports.
The receipt is mentioned but not shown in any photo.

risks.risk: Console may have the 'Blue Light of Death' or a failed HDMI port.
risks.proof: Video of the console booting up and displaying the home screen on a TV.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive may be faulty.
risks.proof: Video of a game disc being inserted, recognized, and launched.

risks.risk: The console may be banned from the PlayStation Network (PSN).
risks.proof: Video showing a successful login to a PSN account on the console.

risks.risk: Controllers may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: Video of the controllers being used to navigate menus or play a game.

proof_requests: Video of the console powered on and connected to a TV showing the dashboard.
Photo of the rear of the console to check the warranty seals.
Video of a disc being inserted and played.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned in the description.
response.reason: A single photo of a powered-off console provides no evidence of functionality. Given the age of the 'Fat' PS4 model and its known hardware risks, proof of operation and seal integrity is mandatory before pricing.
